title: Flat single-cohomology description on an open locus
statement: Let T be a scheme, S a set of points of T, E an object of D(O_T) [def-pc-derived-category], and i a natural number. Assume H^n(E) is zero for every integer n<0 and that each point of S has an open neighbourhood U and a natural rank r such that the restrictions of the natural-degree cohomology sheaves form a finite locally free sheaf in degree i only [def-pc-invertible-in-degree-zero]. Then there is an open W containing S for which H^i(E)|W is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and L(W.ι)^*E [def-pc-derived-pullback] is isomorphic to that restricted sheaf placed in degree i. Restriction uses ordinary module restriction, equivalently open pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. There is no uniform rank assumption, no perfectness assumption, and S may be empty.

source.place: Proof, third paragraph: identify E on the open locus through its cohomology sheaf; first step of lem-pc-derived-pullback-single-cohomology

proof.text: Let W be the union of all opens on which the natural-degree cohomology family of E is finite locally free in degree i in the sense of [def-pc-invertible-in-degree-zero]. The hypothesis puts every point of S in W. For q different from i, restriction of H^q(E) vanishes on each member of this cover, so a section on W whose restrictions are zero is zero by the separated sheaf condition. In negative integer degrees exact open restriction preserves the assumed zero cohomology. Thus the restriction of E to W has cohomology in degree i only.

The restriction of H^i(E) is finite locally free on the covering opens, without any uniform rank requirement. Locally tensoring with it is a finite direct sum of the identity, and therefore preserves exact sequences. Exactness of sheaf sequences is local, so tensoring on W is exact. This is flatness in [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. The argument includes the empty cover and rank zero.

For an open inclusion W.ι, the module pullback of [def-pc-module-pullback] is exact ordinary restriction. Its left derivation [def-pc-derived-pullback] therefore agrees with the exact functor on derived categories, and commutes with cohomology. By the first step it is both cohomologically at least i and at most i. Standard truncation (Mathlib DerivedCategory.exists_iso_singleFunctor_obj_of_isGE_of_isLE, TStructure.lean lines 189-195) identifies it with some single object M in degree i. Apply homology in degree i and the singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorIso to identify M with the restriction of H^i(E); map this isomorphism by singleFunctor and compose. This gives the requested derived restriction isomorphism. The flatness from the second step is the other conjunct.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_flat_single_open_locus
    [∀ Y : Scheme.{u},
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    {T : Scheme.{u}} (S : Set T) (E : schemeDerivedCategory T) (i : ℕ)
    (hneg : ∀ n : ℤ, n < 0 → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings T.toRingedSpace)) n).obj E))
    (hloc : ∀ t ∈ S, ∃ U : T.Opens, t ∈ U ∧ ∃ r : ℕ,
      IsFiniteLocallyFreeInDegree
        (fun q : ℕ ↦ (Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
            (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings T.toRingedSpace)) q).obj E)) i r) :
    ∃ W : T.Opens, S ⊆ W ∧
      SheafOfModules.IsFlat ((Modules.restrictFunctor W.ι).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings T.toRingedSpace)) i).obj E)) ∧
      Nonempty ((derivedPullback W.ι).obj E ≅
        (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings W.toScheme.toRingedSpace)) i).obj
            ((Modules.restrictFunctor W.ι).obj ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
              (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings T.toRingedSpace)) i).obj E)))
